fix_summary: aggregate() in repo_snapshot/experiments/adaptive_v10/run_adaptive_benchmark.py divided the sum of squared deviations by n, i.e. the biased population variance, so the reported std systematically understated seed-to-seed variation. The divisor is now Bessel-corrected (n - 1), computed as 0.0 when n == 1 so the single-seed edge case neither divides by zero nor reports a bogus spread. The public contract is unchanged: the returned key set (mean, std, min, max, n), each key's meaning, the arithmetic mean, the min/max, and the n (which still counts only runs whose metric is present) are all as before. Missing runs are still skipped per metric and never dropped from the list, and the empty-input contract still returns {'mean': None, 'n': 0}.
notes: The task's target defect is the biased estimator; the prompt also names missing-run handling, which the shipped code already performed correctly (per-metric None filtering with no dropping), so that path was left intact and is covered by the public checks. The 1 remaining regression failure is tests/test_adaptive_v10.py::TestSystemComparability::test_all_systems_run_an_episode (AttributeError: 'EwmaAppraisalSystem' object has no attribute 'hazard_hat'), recorded in RealRepoBench-Q2609/tasks/RB-EM-002/baseline_failures.json as a pre-existing failure unrelated to this defect; it is identical before and after the change, so no regression was introduced.
